content: Pura Besakih (the 'Mother Temple') is Bali's largest and holiest Hindu temple complex — 23 separate temples on the slopes of Mount Agung. Belief tradition: Balinese Hindu (Agama Hindu Dharma). Observance type: doctrinal + traditional. Access rules: sarong + sash mandatory (rental available), no entry to inner sanctuaries during ceremonies except for worshippers, no menstruating women per Balinese Hindu convention, tourist entry via a paved path with local-guide encouragement (agree fee first — 100–200k IDR is fair). Entry fee ~60k IDR foreigner.

Pura Luhur Uluwatu is one of the six sad kahyangan (major sea temples) protecting Bali. Belief tradition: Balinese Hindu. Observance type: doctrinal. Dramatic clifftop setting on Bali's south peninsula. Sarong + sash mandatory (included with entry, ~50k IDR foreigner). Macaque monkeys will snatch sunglasses, phones, hats — bag them before entering. The daily Kecak fire dance at sunset (starts ~18:00) is a cultural performance held in a nearby amphitheatre — not part of the temple ritual itself.

Pura Tirta Empul (in Tampaksiring, near Ubud) is the temple of holy spring water — a working Hindu pilgrimage site where Balinese come for melukat (purification bathing) at 30-plus spouts. Belief tradition: Balinese Hindu, active use. Observance type: doctrinal + contemporary practice. Visitors may bathe respectfully: change into a sarong + shorts in the changing area, do not use the two spouts reserved for funeral cleansing (marked; ask staff), do not photograph individuals mid-prayer, women should not enter the pools during menstruation.
